entry.title: thinking about weekly reviews
entry.content:
I spent a while getting weekly reviews wrong. Here is the version that works for me.

why it matters

Weekly reviews shows up across productivity work more often than it deserves credit for. The details are small, but they compound.

what works for me

  • Most of the value is in deleting, not adding.
  • The fix that survives is the one the next person can understand.
  • Name it after what it does, not after how it does it.

None of this is a law. It is just the shape that kept working after enough mistakes.

entry.title: rethinking weekly reviews
entry.content:
Short post: weekly reviews is one of those things that looks simple until it isn’t.

why it matters

Weekly reviews shows up across productivity work more often than it deserves credit for. The details are small, but they compound.

what works for me

  • Start with the smallest thing that works, then make it boring on purpose.
  • The fix that survives is the one the next person can understand.
  • Make the default path the correct path so nobody has to remember the rule.

None of this is a law. It is just the shape that kept working after enough mistakes.

entry.title: rethinking weekly reviews
entry.content:
I keep coming back to weekly reviews, so here are the notes I wish I had earlier.

why it matters

Weekly reviews shows up across productivity work more often than it deserves credit for. The details are small, but they compound.

what works for me

  • Measure before you change anything; intuition is a poor profiler.
  • Write it down once, link to it everywhere.
  • Optimise for the reader who shows up six months from now with no context.

None of this is a law. It is just the shape that kept working after enough mistakes.
